A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 19-page EfficientNav paper, including Appendices A–H. Complete text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable assessment; pages 2–19 are identical.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original HM3D navigation, latency, and ablation results. Appendix E provides additional experimental comparisons of retrieval models.

after.justification: The original navigation, latency, and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix E are retained unchanged.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain identical discrete memory caching, attention-based memory clustering, and semantics-aware retrieval procedures. The architectures and planning examples in the appendices are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate zero-shot indoor object-goal navigation on HM3D using Habitat. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2, 3, 6, and 8, including the navigation baselines, vLLM, sparse-attention methods, and alternative retrieval models.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same evaluation procedures, SR/SPL and latency metrics, four planner variants, and deployment settings. The memory-budget experiments and appendix settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 4, memory-budget analysis in Table 5, cache and latency analyses, and retrieval-model ablation in Appendix E/Table 8 are identical.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains the disclosure of 15 navigation trials per final goal with different starting points. Run information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical testing are unchanged throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, EfficientNav-34b retains SR 80.0 and SPL 41.5 in Table 2, and RtL 0.87s and E2EL 12.51s in Table 3.

T1.justification: The group-selection knapsack formulation in Equations (1)–(2) and the attention and KV-cache mathematics in Appendix A are identical. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and performance claims. The revised code-availability statement changes access information rather than the claimed research contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations of performance and caching behavior are unchanged. Section 5 and Appendices G–H retain the same limitations concerning latency, cloud communication/privacy, and specialized or hazardous environments.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces 'Our code will be released soon' with a code-availability statement and a link to the PKU-SEC-Lab/EfficientNav repository. Implementation, architecture, and hardware disclosures elsewhere remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons positioning EfficientNav against prior research, and all 89 reference entries are unchanged.

P1.justification: Only the abstract's code-availability sentence and the arXiv version/date stamp are edited. The remaining prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure are identical.

P2.justification: The repository address adds one line to the abstract and slightly shifts the first-page text layout. All figures and tables are unchanged, and pages 2–19 render identically.

improvement.justification: Providing a specific repository link instead of promising a future release modestly improves code-access and reproducibility information. The scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
